newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: StanChart to close Singapore broking firm.
newsitem.headline: StanChart to close Singapore broking firm.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank (StanChart) said on Friday it was closing down its securities firm in Singapore by the end of December, 1996.
Alan Mole, StanChart's regional head of corporate affairs, Southeast Asia, told Reuters that its Singapore securities firm had to wind up because the licence was not transferable.

The British bank had sold most of its broking interests and operations in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, China, Thailand, United Kingdom and United States to Thai brokerage Nava Finance & Securities. Nava could not take over the Singapore securities firm as the Singapore licence was not transferable.
"Our (broking firm) licence expires at the end of this year, therefore we have no alternative but to close Standard Chartered Securities," said Mole.
"The bank has made it clear some time ago that it was concentrating on its core banking activities," he said.
Mole said the Singapore securities firm had about 20 staff and compensation would vary, depending on length of service.
Chris Mallows, chief executive officer of Nava SC Securities in Hong Kong, said: "Nava group is applying for a licence" to operate in Singapore.
